text:
maria: quick share — ran a focused microbenchmark for q4_h L2-13B on small payloads (batch=1, gen len ~16). comparing FlashAttn v2, FlashAttn v3 and Triton vendor kernels across eu-west1 (A100) and apac-sin (H100). @jon @zheng can you eyeball these?

bench-bot: run_id=172845-qa1 summary (p95 latency, single-token warm):
- eu-west1 (A100): flashv3=48ms, flashv2=66ms, triton=57ms
- apac-sin (H100): flashv3=44ms, flashv2=60ms, triton=50ms
- throughput (tokens/s, sustained small-batch): eu flashv3=210, triton=180, flashv2=150
(links: https://bench.redwood/172845/summary)

jon: thanks — interesting that flashv3 wins both regions but gap is smaller on H100. did you do cold vs warm p95?

maria: warm vs cold: cold p95s are ~1.6x higher across the board, but relative ordering stays same. warmup uses our standard 5-request warmup.

zheng: can you paste the exact command? want to reproduce with triton flags we use in prod.

maria: sure:
```bash
./run_bench --model llama2-13b --quant q4_h --kernel flashv3 --batch 1 --gen 16 --warmup 5 --region eu-west1 --export p95,throughput
```

maria: for triton I used our vendor-default config (dynamic batching off, cuBLAS path) — will attach config in the gist.

eva: did you run any evals for generation quality after q4_h? we should ensure flashv3 quant path doesn't regress tokenization or token ordering.

maria: ran a tiny eval on our smoke prompts (50 prompts): sacreBLEU-like metric difference <0.2 pts between kernels; perplexity identical to 1 decimal. no visible hallucination spikes.

jon: good. what's the memory headroom on H100 vs A100 at q4_h? important for packing multiple concurrent small requests.

bench-bot: mem snapshot (resident) during flashv3 run: eu-west1(A100)=27GB used of 40GB, apac-sin(H100)=23GB of 80GB. pack factor suggests we can host ~1.6x more concurrent small sessions in apac.

zheng: ok CPU overhead? triton path still cheaper CPU-wise for small batches because it avoids our flashv3 shim copies. do we have CPU-ms numbers?

maria: CPU ms (per request): flashv3=5ms, triton=3.5ms, flashv2=6ms. so tradeoff: flashv3 uses slightly more CPU but wins on GPU kernel runtime.

samir: TL;DR from infra perspective: flashv3 is default winner for latency-sensitive, small-batch q4_h in eu and apac. but we need to guard for microbursts and CPU pressure in apac when load spikes.

jon: propose rule: enable flashv3 default for q4_h on A100/H100 for routes with p95 SLO < 80ms and median payload size < 40 tokens. fallback to triton for routes with high concurrency/noisy neighbors. add hysteresis: require 3 consecutive intervals of degraded p95 before switching kernel.

eva: also add a quality check step in rollout: run eval set (100 prompts) and compare top-1 token agreement vs baseline; abort switch if disagreement >1.0%.

maria: agreed. I'll open a rollout PR with canary config: 1% traffic eu-west1 flashv3 enable tomorrow, 1% apac-sin next week. will include metric dashboards: p95, qps, cpu-ms, mem, token-agreement.

zheng: for reproducing triton config, attaching snippet (in gist). also recommend we test triton with a tuned kernel that uses split-warp GEMM — might close the gap on H100.

samir: action items:
- maria: PR + canary config + dashboard (due EOD today)
- jon: write hysteresis + fallback playbook for kernel switch (due Wed)
- zheng: run vendor-tuned triton sweep on H100 instance and report (due Fri)
- eva: prepare eval harness for token-agreement check (due Thu)

jon: one note — if CPU pressure becomes limiting in apac during canary, we should consider enabling async-copy path in flashv3 (experimental) with a flag. it's faster but needs careful mem-safety checks.

maria: noted. will include that as opt-in in canary.

samir: thanks team. overall looks safe to prefer flashv3 for small-batch q4_h but we'll gate rollout behind the quality and cpu checks. :thumbsup:

maria: filing the PR now: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops/pull/812

jon: great — thanks everyone.
